name: Nu Holdings
thesis: Latin America's leading digital bank (Brazil + Mexico + Colombia). In Brazil — now a mature, ~60%+ penetrated market — the story shifts from customer adds to monetization: ARPAC compounding as cohorts deepen product penetration into credit card, personal loan, investments, and insurance, with risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk) expanding as cost-to-serve stays near-zero. In Mexico and Colombia, total customer count remains the primary signal — these are the new acquisition engines, compounding on network effects and low CAC, but Mexico's credit book mix is the watch-item (unhedged expansion if it grows >50% QoQ). Bet: durable Brazil profitability — ROE crossing 30% on a consolidated basis, held above a 25% floor — funds growth-market expansion while consolidated revenue growth holds the 25%+ track and CET1 stays above 13%. Thesis breaks if ROE sustains below 25% for two quarters, risk-adjusted NIM contracts YoY for two quarters, revenue growth decelerates by more than 80% versus the prior-year same quarter, consolidated NPL 15d+ deteriorates YoY by more than 150bps for two same-fiscal-quarter prints, or net customer adds fall below 5M/Q while Brazil flagship-product penetration rolls over QoQ.
key_driver: Customer count × ARPAC × NIM with NPL controlled
chart_priorities: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
Capital adequacy ratio (CET1 / Basel III total)
Credit exposure by product x country

tier_1_kpis.name: ROE (annualized, consolidated)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Consolidated ROE <25% for 2 consecutive Qs (thesis bet is ROE crossing 30% durably)

tier_1_kpis.name: Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Risk-adjusted NIM contracts YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (cost of risk outrunning NIM expansion)

tier_1_kpis.name: Capital adequacy ratio (CET1 / Basel III total)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Capital ratio falls below 13% OR drops >150bps QoQ without explicit growth-deployment rationale (cushion erosion)

tier_1_kpis.name: NPL 15d+ ratio (consolidated total: early-stage 15-90d + severe 90d+, YoY-tracked)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Total NPL (15d+ consolidated) YoY deterioration >150bps for 2 consecutive Qs in the same fiscal quarter — YoY framing controls for LatAm consumer-credit seasonality; absolute level is allowed to drift with the evolving underwriting mix, but rapid YoY worsening signals a credit-cycle break rather than a seasonal pattern

tier_1_kpis.name: Monthly ARPAC (USD)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: ARPAC growth <15% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_1_kpis.name: Product penetration by country (% of customers using each product, Brazil/Mexico/Colombia x credit card/personal loan/investments/insurance)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Brazil flagship-product penetration declines QoQ for 2 consecutive Qs OR Mexico penetration ramp stalls

tier_1_kpis.name: Credit exposure by product x country (loan book mix: credit card / personal loan / SMB / FGTS, split Brazil/Mexico/Colombia)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Single-product concentration >60% of consolidated book OR Mexico credit book grows >50% QoQ (unhedged expansion risk)

tier_1_kpis.name: Total customers (millions)
tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Net adds <5M per quarter for 2 consecutive Qs

tier_2_kpis.name: NPL 90d+ by product (credit card vs personal loan vs SMB) — early warning on which product cycle is breaking

thesis_breakers_qualitative: ROE fails to durably cross 30% / drifts below 25% (exceptional-profitability thesis breaks)
Risk-adjusted NIM stops expanding (pricing power vs. credit-cost balance lost)
Capital cushion erodes without growth-deployment rationale

Total NPL (15d+ consolidated) deteriorates YoY beyond ~150bps in the same fiscal quarter — i.e. worsening that exceeds seasonality and is not explained by deliberate underwriting-mix shifts (credit-cycle break)

break_rules.kpi_name: Revenue YoY Growth Deceleration (YoY of YoY growth rate)
break_rules.narrative: Revenue YoY growth rate decelerates by more than 80% compared to the same quarter a year prior (e.g. prior-year same-Q YoY growth of 30% collapsing to <6% this Q). Thesis bet is consolidated revenue growth holding 25%+; a single-quarter 80%+ collapse in the growth rate itself signals the growth engine has stalled, even if absolute revenue is still nominally positive YoY.
Consolidated ROE below 25% for 2 consecutive quarters — thesis bet is durable ROE crossing 30%; sustained sub-25% means the exceptional-profitability story is broken.
Risk-adjusted NIM (NIM minus cost of risk) contracting YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — either pricing power is eroding or cost of risk is outrunning yield, undermining the expanding-spread thesis.
Capital ratio below 13% — prudent-cushion thesis breaks; well-capitalized banks in LatAm typically run 14-18%, sub-13% signals either aggressive deployment or stress.

Consolidated NPL (15d+ total, covering both early-stage 15-90d and severe 90d+) deteriorating YoY by more than 150bps (1.5pp) for 2 consecutive quarters in the same fiscal quarter comparison. YoY framing rather than absolute level — the underwriting mix legitimately shifts the steady-state NPL ratio (more credit card / SMB / FGTS each have different baseline NPLs), so absolute thresholds break as the book evolves. business_model_rules.narrative: 90d+ NPL > 7% for 2Q — credit-quality break; their underwriting thesis depends on the 5-6% historical range holding.
Monthly ARPAC < $10 for 2Q — cross-sell stalling; expanding ARPAC is the unit-economics flywheel.
Activity rate < 82% for 2Q — customers becoming dormant; engagement-flywheel signal.
15-90d NPL > 5% for 2Q — leading indicator of cohort credit deterioration; fires 1-2Q before 90d+ trips.
